rationale: No acceptance spec (compact profile, no-spec mode); confidence is low. 6 blocking findings confirmed against source: one critical UI-hang in runner-bridge.js (exitP awaited with no timeout), four concurrency bugs in pty_kill (spurious-wakeup false Ok, missed pre-exit flag check, ESRCH not tolerated, no run_id guard), and one JS listener leak. 0 deferred, 0 dismissed.

findings.title: pty_kill lacks run_id guard
findings.problem: pty_kill takes no run_id parameter; it kills whichever PTY slot is occupied, ignoring which session the caller intended to terminate. The state tuple stores the run_id but pty_kill discards it (matches on `(_, h)`).
findings.impact: If a new PTY session starts between a caller's kill decision and the actual kill invocation, the new session is terminated instead. The JS bridge passes no id to pty_kill, making this race undetectable at the call site.
findings.recommendation: Add an optional `run_id: Option<String>` parameter to pty_kill; early-return Ok(()) when the slot's id does not match. Update the JS bridge (runner-bridge.js:140) accordingly. If the id-agnostic design is intentional per the 'No concurrent-spawn guard' constraint, document the accepted race in a code comment.

findings.title: kill() not tolerant of ESRCH after slot release
findings.problem: The state Mutex is released at line 200 before kill() is called at line 205. Between these two points the child can exit naturally; kill() then returns an OS ESRCH error, which is mapped directly to InstallerError::Pty and propagated to the caller.
findings.impact: pty_kill returns an error when the child is already gone — the desired final state — causing callers to treat a benign race as a failure and potentially surfacing a spurious error in the UI.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the kill() call: `.or_else(|e| if is_no_such_process_error(&e) { Ok(()) } else { Err(e) })`. Implement `is_no_such_process_error` to match the platform error code (ESRCH on Unix, ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE / ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED on Windows).

findings.title: condvar wait skips pre-exit flag check
findings.problem: wait_timeout is entered without first inspecting the exit flag. If the child has already exited and called notify_all before the Mutex is acquired here, the notification is lost and wait_timeout blocks for the full 5 seconds.
findings.impact: pty_kill unnecessarily stalls a tokio spawn_blocking thread for 5 seconds after a fast-exiting child, delaying the caller and wasting a thread-pool slot.
findings.recommendation: After `let guard = lk.lock().unwrap();`, add `if *guard { return Ok(()); }` before calling wait_timeout.

findings.title: wait_timeout not guarded against spurious wakeup
findings.problem: cv.wait_timeout can return on a spurious wakeup with timed_out() returning false. The subsequent check `if timed_out.timed_out() && !*timed_out_guard` only returns an error on a real timeout; a spurious wakeup causes the function to return Ok(()) without verifying the exit flag.
findings.impact: pty_kill incorrectly reports success while the child process is still running; callers believe the PTY is terminated when it is not, potentially leaving a zombie shell holding PTY resources.
findings.recommendation: Replace cv.wait_timeout with cv.wait_timeout_while(guard, Duration::from_secs(5), |exited| !*exited). That variant loops on spurious wakeups and only returns when the exit flag is true or the timeout elapses.

findings.title: pty-data listener leaks when exit-listen throws
findings.problem: dataUnlisten is registered at line 122 outside the try block; if the subsequent listen('engine:pty-exit') call at line 126 throws, the error propagates before the try block is entered, so the finally block never runs and dataUnlisten is never called.
findings.impact: The engine:pty-data listener stays active indefinitely, invoking onData for every subsequent PTY run. Repeated spawnPty calls stack up additional leaked listeners with no cleanup path.
findings.recommendation: Move both listen calls inside the try block (register exitUnlisten first, then dataUnlisten, then invoke spawn_pty). Add a catch clause that calls dataUnlisten?.() and exitUnlisten?.() before rethrowing, so partial registration is always cleaned up.

findings.title: spawnPty awaits exitP with no timeout
findings.problem: exitP resolves only when engine:pty-exit fires for the matching id. If Tauri state is lost, the app is backgrounded mid-run, or emit silently fails after spawn_pty returns, the promise never settles.
findings.impact: spawnPty hangs indefinitely; the install orchestration is blocked and the UI freezes with no recovery path short of an app restart.
findings.recommendation: Race exitP against a rejection timeout: `const code = await Promise.race([exitP, new Promise((_, reject) => setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('pty exit timeout')), PTY_TIMEOUT_MS))]);`. Ensure both exitUnlisten and dataUnlisten are called in the finally block regardless of which branch wins.
